// Code generated by w17. DO NOT EDIT.
//
// e2erunner — the project's e2e suite as a standalone binary. Build with
// `go test -c -o e2erunner .` (a no-Go consumer does this via the
// Dockerfile), then run:
//
//	./e2erunner -target http://localhost:8080 [-domain app] [-transport rest[,admin]] [-mcp http://localhost:8081/mcp]
//	            [-endpoint billing/rest=http://localhost:8090 ...]
//
// The MCP endpoint is its OWN listener (:8081 by default, see
// <PREFIX>_MCP_LISTEN_ADDR) and serves on /mcp. This line used to say
// 8080/mcp — the REST port with the right path — which is an address
// that has never existed: the REST gateway 404s every path it does not
// route, so following the hint produced "404 page not found" with
// nothing pointing at the port.
//
// Each (domain, transport) scenario is a Test function running its whole
// ordered step sequence; --domain/--transport filter which scenarios run.
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/wandering-compiler/sdk/go/tooling/e2e/dpope2e"
	"github.com/wandering-compiler/sdk/go/tooling/e2e/runner"
	"github.com/wandering-compiler/sdk/go/tooling/e2e/stress"
)

var (
	targetFlag    string
	mcpFlag       string
	adminFlag     string
	domainFlag    string
	transportFlag string
	formatFlag    string

	// requireAllFlag makes a run FULL: a scenario it selects whose
	// transport has no endpoint fails instead of skipping. w17ctl test sets
	// it (E2E_REQUIRE_ALL): a suite the project bakes is coverage it
	// declares, and an endpoint discovery that found nothing must not turn
	// it into a green run of the rest. A transport is left out by name
	// (-transport); a bare `go test` keeps the skip.
	requireAllFlag bool
)

// endpoints are the domains' own addresses (-endpoint, E2E_ENDPOINTS), for
// a project whose domains serve their surfaces from different binaries —
// w17ctl test finds them in the stack. A surface whose domain has no entry
// is reached at -target, -mcp or -admin.
var endpoints = endpointFlag{}

// endpointFlag is the repeatable -endpoint <domain>/<surface>=<value>: the
// surface is rest, mcp or admin (a base URL), or rest-origin or
// admin-origin (the public origin device proofs name for that surface).
type endpointFlag map[string]string

func (e endpointFlag) String() string { return "" }

func (e endpointFlag) Set(v string) error {
	key, value, ok := strings.Cut(v, "=")
	domain, surface, okKey := strings.Cut(key, "/")
	if !ok || !okKey || domain == "" || value == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("-endpoint %q: want <domain>/<surface>=<url>", v)
	}
	switch surface {
	case "rest", "mcp", "admin", "rest-origin", "admin-origin":
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("-endpoint %q: unknown surface %q (want rest, mcp, admin, rest-origin or admin-origin)", v, surface)
	}
	e[key] = value
	return nil
}

// endpoint is the address the run gave for domain's surface, else def.
func endpoint(domain, surface, def string) string {
	if v, ok := endpoints[domain+"/"+surface]; ok {
		return v
	}
	return def
}

// The public origins device proofs name (dpope2e.WithOrigin): the
// gateway's and the admin's <PREFIX>_DPOP_ORIGIN, for a run that reaches
// them at other addresses — w17ctl test dials ports it published itself.
var (
	dpopOriginFlag      string
	adminDPoPOriginFlag string
)

var (
	stressFlag        bool
	stressConcurrency int
	stressDuration    string
	stressTotal       int
)

// stressEnabled gates the generated stress tests on the -stress flag, so a
// bare `go test` runs the e2e suite without ever hammering the target.
var stressEnabled bool

func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
	flag.StringVar(&targetFlag, "target", envOr("E2E_TARGET", "http://localhost:8080"), "REST base URL of the deployed gateway")
	flag.StringVar(&mcpFlag, "mcp", envOr("E2E_MCP", ""), "MCP endpoint URL (set when running MCP scenarios)")
	flag.StringVar(&adminFlag, "admin", envOr("E2E_ADMIN", ""), "admin gateway base URL (set when running admin scenarios)")
	flag.StringVar(&domainFlag, "domain", os.Getenv("E2E_DOMAIN"), "run only this domain (empty = all)")
	flag.StringVar(&transportFlag, "transport", os.Getenv("E2E_TRANSPORT"), "run only these transports: rest, mcp, admin, or a comma-separated list of them (empty = all)")
	flag.StringVar(&formatFlag, "format", envOr("E2E_FORMAT", "text"), "per-step output: text (✓/✗ checklist) or json (one NDJSON record per step)")
	flag.BoolVar(&requireAllFlag, "require-all", os.Getenv("E2E_REQUIRE_ALL") != "", "fail a selected scenario whose transport has no endpoint instead of skipping it (w17ctl test sets it; leave a transport out with -transport)")
	flag.Var(endpoints, "endpoint", "a domain's own address, <domain>/<surface>=<url> with surface rest, mcp or admin (or rest-origin / admin-origin, the public origin its device proofs name); repeatable, and E2E_ENDPOINTS takes a comma-separated list")
	for _, v := range strings.Split(os.Getenv("E2E_ENDPOINTS"), ",") {
		if v = strings.TrimSpace(v); v == "" {
			continue
		}
		if err := endpoints.Set(v); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "e2e: E2E_ENDPOINTS: %v\n", err)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
	}
	flag.StringVar(&dpopOriginFlag, "dpop-origin", os.Getenv("E2E_DPOP_ORIGIN"), "public origin (scheme://host[:port], no path) of the REST gateway — its <PREFIX>_DPOP_ORIGIN — that device proofs name, when -target reaches it at another address (empty = the origin of -target)")
	flag.StringVar(&adminDPoPOriginFlag, "admin-dpop-origin", os.Getenv("E2E_ADMIN_DPOP_ORIGIN"), "public origin (scheme://host[:port], no path) of the admin — its <PREFIX>_DPOP_ORIGIN — that device proofs name, when -admin reaches it at another address (empty = the origin of -admin)")
	flag.BoolVar(&stressFlag, "stress", os.Getenv("E2E_STRESS") != "", "run stress/load presets (off by default so a bare go test doesn't hammer the target)")
	flag.IntVar(&stressConcurrency, "stress.concurrency", 0, "override every preset's worker count (0 = use the plan)")
	flag.StringVar(&stressDuration, "stress.duration", "", "override every preset's run window, e.g. 30s (empty = use the plan)")
	flag.IntVar(&stressTotal, "stress.total", 0, "override every preset's total_requests (0 = use the plan)")
	flag.Parse()
	runner.SetFormat(formatFlag)
	stressEnabled = stressFlag
	// An override that does not parse is refused, not ignored: ignoring it
	// ran the plan's window while the operator believed theirs was in force.
	if stressDuration != "" {
		if d, err := time.ParseDuration(stressDuration); err != nil || d <= 0 {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "e2e: -stress.duration %q: want a positive duration with a unit, e.g. 30s or 2m\n", stressDuration)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
	}
	code := m.Run()
	// Skipped, and said so: a skip only -test.v would show reads, in a
	// green run, exactly like a suite that has no MCP scenarios.
	if n := mcpDeviceSkipped.Load(); n > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "e2e: %d step(s) in %d MCP scenario(s) skipped: %s\n", mcpDeviceSkippedSteps.Load(), n, mcpDeviceSkip)
	}
	// A run that asserted NOTHING must never exit 0. Every scenario skips
	// on its own (filtered out, or its transport has no endpoint), and
	// `go test` calls an all-skipped package a PASS — so a mistyped
	// -domain, or -transport admin against a stack whose admin endpoint was
	// never discovered, reported success while checking zero steps. The
	// suite is the thing that knows how many scenarios it has, so the
	// verdict belongs here rather than in whatever drove it.
	if code == 0 {
		if err := requireScenariosRan(); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "e2e: %v\n", err)
			code = 1
		}
	}
	// The same rule for PART of a run. A scenario the run selected, with its
	// transport's endpoint given, that cannot run is coverage the suite
	// declares and did not deliver — when an auth upgrade started binding
	// devices, every MCP scenario of a project went, and the run still said
	// PASS beside its REST results. Leaving MCP out is the project's call,
	// made in the run's own arguments, not something an upgrade decides.
	if code == 0 && mcpDeviceSkipped.Load() > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "e2e: FAIL — %d step(s) of MCP scenarios did not run, so this run did not test them. "+
			"Make them runnable (declare (w17.mcp_api).oauth), or leave MCP out of the run on purpose: "+
			"-transport rest,admin (w17ctl test --transport rest,admin)\n", mcpDeviceSkippedSteps.Load())
		code = 1
	}
	os.Exit(code)
}

// totalScenarios is the number of scenarios this suite was generated with —
// baked, because at run time an all-skipped suite and an empty one look
// identical, and only the empty one is allowed to pass without running.
const totalScenarios = 4

// How many scenarios passed the --domain/--transport filter, and how many
// of those also had their transport's endpoint configured (i.e. actually
// ran). Written from the test functions, which `go test` may run in
// parallel.
var (
	scenariosMatched atomic.Int64
	scenariosRan     atomic.Int64
)

// gate is every scenario's preamble: apply the --domain/--transport filter,
// then require the transport's endpoint. Skipping on either is deliberate
// (a bare `go test` with no live targets must not fail the MCP/admin
// suites) — what is NOT deliberate is a whole run made of those skips, so
// both outcomes are counted for requireScenariosRan; and a FULL run
// (-require-all) fails a selected scenario with no endpoint outright.
func gate(t *testing.T, domain, transport string, steps []runner.Step) map[string]runner.Caller {
	t.Helper()
	if !selected(domain, transport) {
		t.Skip("filtered out by --domain/--transport")
	}
	scenariosMatched.Add(1)
	// Counted only when there is an MCP endpoint to skip: without one the
	// scenario is skipped below as not configured, like any other.
	if transport == "mcp" && endpoint(domain, "mcp", mcpFlag) != "" && restSigns(domain) && !mcpOAuth(domain) {
		mcpDeviceSkipped.Add(1)
		mcpDeviceSkippedSteps.Add(int64(len(steps)))
		t.Skip(mcpDeviceSkip)
	}
	cs := callers(domain)
	if _, ok := cs[transport]; !ok && requireAllFlag {
		t.Fatalf("transport %q not configured, and this run requires every scenario it selects (-require-all) — "+
			"the suite declares this one, so a run without it did not test it: set its target flag (-target / -mcp / -admin, "+
			"or -endpoint %s/%s=<url>), or leave the transport out on purpose with -transport", transport, domain, transport)
	}
	if _, ok := cs[transport]; !ok {
		t.Skipf("transport %q not configured — set its target flag (-target / -mcp / -admin, or -endpoint %s/%s=<url>)", transport, domain, transport)
	}
	scenariosRan.Add(1)
	return cs
}

// requireScenariosRan turns "nothing ran" into a failure, naming which of
// the two causes it was so the message points at the fix rather than at the
// symptom.
func requireScenariosRan() error {
	if totalScenarios == 0 || scenariosRan.Load() > 0 {
		return nil
	}
	if scenariosMatched.Load() == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("no scenario matched -domain=%q -transport=%q — %d scenario(s) exist and none of them ran, so this run verified nothing",
			domainFlag, transportFlag, totalScenarios)
	}
	if mcpDeviceSkipped.Load() == scenariosMatched.Load() {
		return fmt.Errorf("every scenario matching -domain=%q -transport=%q was skipped: each is an MCP scenario of a surface that binds devices (%s) — this run verified nothing",
			domainFlag, transportFlag, mcpDeviceSkip)
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("every scenario matching -domain=%q -transport=%q was skipped: its transport has no endpoint configured — pass -mcp / -admin (or -target for rest); this run verified nothing",
		domainFlag, transportFlag)
}

// selected reports whether a scenario passes the --domain/--transport filter.
// -transport names one transport or a comma-separated list: a run that
// leaves one out says so in its arguments.
func selected(domain, transport string) bool {
	if domainFlag != "" && domainFlag != domain {
		return false
	}
	if transportFlag == "" {
		return true
	}
	for _, t := range strings.Split(transportFlag, ",") {
		if strings.TrimSpace(t) == transport {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// callers builds the transport clients of a scenario of domain from the
// flags. MCP is wired only when an endpoint is configured. The REST and
// admin callers of a surface that binds devices sign every request that
// presents a token or mints one (DPoP); MCP presents a Bearer token as
// before, which is why such a surface's MCP scenarios are skipped (gate).
func callers(domain string) map[string]runner.Caller {
	rest := runner.NewRESTCaller(endpoint(domain, "rest", targetFlag), nil)
	if restSigns(domain) {
		rest = rest.WithSigner(restSigner(domain))
	}
	c := map[string]runner.Caller{"rest": rest}
	if u := endpoint(domain, "mcp", mcpFlag); u != "" {
		mcp := runner.NewMCPCaller(u, nil)
		// An MCP surface that is an OAuth protected resource takes an MCP
		// access token, never the REST session: the caller exchanges the
		// session for one through the authorization server.
		switch domain {
		case "app":
			mcp = mcp.WithOAuth(runner.MCPOAuth{Issuer: endpoint(domain, "rest", targetFlag), REST: rest, Get: &runner.Endpoint{Ref: "auth.AuthService.GetOAuthAuthorization", Transport: "rest", AuthRequired: true, HTTPMethod: "GET", PathTemplate: "/api/v1/auth/oauth/authorizations/{request_id}", PathParams: []string{"request_id"}}, Approve: &runner.Endpoint{Ref: "auth.AuthService.ApproveOAuthAuthorization", Transport: "rest", AuthRequired: true, HTTPMethod: "POST", PathTemplate: "/api/v1/auth/oauth/authorizations/{request_id}/approve", PathParams: []string{"request_id"}, BodyField: "*"}})
		}
		c["mcp"] = mcp
	}
	// admin is HTTP/REST-shaped (the admin bundle's /admin/api/... routes),
	// so it reuses the REST caller against the admin gateway's base URL.
	if u := endpoint(domain, "admin", adminFlag); u != "" {
		admin := runner.NewRESTCaller(u, nil)
		if adminSigns(domain) {
			admin = admin.WithSigner(adminSigner(domain))
		}
		c["admin"] = admin
	}
	return c
}

// Device keys (DPoP, RFC 9449). A surface whose auth method binds tokens
// to device keys accepts a token only with a proof by the key its sign-in
// was signed with; the runner makes a key per simulated device and signs
// with it. One signer per origin the proofs name, a device's key the same
// on all of them.
var signers sync.Map // origin → *dpope2e.Signer

// restSigner and adminSigner are the signers of domain's REST and admin
// surfaces.
func restSigner(domain string) *dpope2e.Signer {
	return signerFor(domain, "rest", dpopOriginFlag)
}

func adminSigner(domain string) *dpope2e.Signer {
	return signerFor(domain, "admin", adminDPoPOriginFlag)
}

// signerFor returns the signer whose proofs name the origin of domain's
// surface: the one the run gave for it (-endpoint <domain>/<surface>-origin),
// else the address it is dialled at when the run gave the domain its own,
// else the surface's -dpop-origin flag, which belongs to -target / -admin.
func signerFor(domain, surface, flagOrigin string) *dpope2e.Signer {
	origin := flagOrigin
	if _, own := endpoints[domain+"/"+surface]; own {
		origin = ""
	}
	origin = endpoint(domain, surface+"-origin", origin)
	s, _ := signers.LoadOrStore(origin, newSigner(origin))
	return s.(*dpope2e.Signer)
}

// newSigner returns a signer whose proofs name origin, or the origin of
// the caller's own base URL when origin is empty.
func newSigner(origin string) *dpope2e.Signer {
	if origin == "" {
		return dpope2e.New()
	}
	return dpope2e.New(dpope2e.WithOrigin(origin))
}

// restSigns reports whether domain's REST surface binds tokens to device
// keys (its auth method's response declares device_id).
func restSigns(domain string) bool {
	return domain == "app"
}

// adminSigns reports whether domain's admin binds tokens to device keys
// (its user lookup's response declares device_id).
func adminSigns(domain string) bool {
	return domain == "app"
}

// mcpOAuth reports whether domain's MCP surface is an OAuth protected
// resource: its MCP caller exchanges the session for an MCP token, so its
// scenarios run although the surface binds devices.
func mcpOAuth(domain string) bool {
	return domain == "app"
}

// mcpDeviceSkip is why an MCP scenario of a surface that binds devices
// does not run: such a gateway refuses the REST session on MCP, and only a
// surface that is an OAuth protected resource gives the caller another
// token. mcpDeviceSkipped counts those scenarios and mcpDeviceSkippedSteps
// their steps — the number to report, since one scenario is a domain's
// whole MCP suite and "1 scenario" can be dozens of steps; it counts them
// as the run's [n/N] does, the REST sign-ins of a pre: included.
const mcpDeviceSkip = "the surface binds tokens to device keys and its MCP is no OAuth protected resource, so the MCP caller has only the REST session, which its gateway refuses — declare (w17.mcp_api).oauth"

var mcpDeviceSkipped, mcpDeviceSkippedSteps atomic.Int64

// signsREST and signsAdmin say which surfaces of this suite sign device
// proofs in some domain. Nothing here reads them: w17ctl test does, to know
// which public origins the suite needs from the stack.
const (
	signsREST  = true
	signsAdmin = true
)

func envOr(key, def string) string {
	if v := os.Getenv(key); v != "" {
		return v
	}
	return def
}

// eventSubscriber taps the gateway's /w17-events SSE broadcast for steps
// that carry an `await_event:` assertion. It targets the REST base (public
// events surface on the REST gateway regardless of the triggering step's
// transport); the per-step baked Path selects the route.
func eventSubscriber(domain string) runner.EventSubscriber {
	s := runner.NewSSESubscriber(endpoint(domain, "rest", targetFlag), nil)
	if restSigns(domain) {
		s = s.WithSigner(restSigner(domain))
	}
	return s
}

// streamCaller opens a streaming ENDPOINT for steps that carry an
// `expect_stream:` assertion — a server-streaming RPC routed as SSE. It is
// not the same thing as eventSubscriber above: that one taps the project's
// public event bus, this one opens the endpoint and reads what the endpoint
// itself sends.
func streamCaller(domain string) runner.StreamCaller {
	c := runner.NewSSEStreamCaller(endpoint(domain, "rest", targetFlag), nil)
	if restSigns(domain) {
		c = c.WithSigner(restSigner(domain))
	}
	return c
}

// applyStressOverrides lets the -stress.* flags override a baked plan for
// ad-hoc runs (tune concurrency / window without regenerating). A count
// override and a duration override are mutually exclusive — the last one
// set wins, matching the plan's own one-stop-condition rule.
func applyStressOverrides(p *stress.Plan) {
	if stressConcurrency > 0 {
		p.Concurrency = stressConcurrency
	}
	if stressTotal > 0 {
		p.TotalRequests = stressTotal
		p.Duration = 0
	}
	if stressDuration != "" {
		if d, err := time.ParseDuration(stressDuration); err == nil {
			p.Duration = d
			p.TotalRequests = 0
		}
	}
}

// loadCaller builds the fasthttp load caller against the REST target (the
// fast path used only by the load phase; setup/teardown use the asserting
// callers()).
func loadCaller(domain string, concurrency int, timeout time.Duration) *stress.LoadCaller {
	lc := stress.NewLoadCaller(endpoint(domain, "rest", targetFlag), concurrency, timeout)
	if restSigns(domain) {
		lc = lc.WithSigner(restSigner(domain))
	}
	return lc
}
